plan: This is a second-price auction (I pay the second-highest bid if I win), so the dominant strategy is to bid exactly my true value of $47. Bidding higher risks paying more than the item is worth to me if I win; bidding lower risks losing auctions I could have profitably won. With no information suggesting collusion or unusual competitor behavior, truthful bidding maximizes my expected profit.

This is a second-price auction (Vickrey-style): I pay the second-highest bid if I win, not my own bid. The dominant strategy in this format is to bid exactly my true value, since bidding higher risks overpaying relative to my value if I win, and bidding lower only reduces my chances of winning without changing what I pay. With no prior history to adjust for, truthful bidding maximizes expected profit.

This is a second-price auction format where the winner pays the second-highest bid, not their own bid. In this setup, bidding my true value is the dominant strategy - I win whenever my value exceeds the second-highest bid, and I pay less than my value in that case, ensuring non-negative profit. Bidding higher than my value risks paying more than the item is worth to me. Bidding lower risks losing auctions I should win. Therefore, I will bid exactly my true value of $36.
